set to 400. For all models, we inject adapters or switchers in all 12 layers of BERT. All experiments are run on the single GPU at an 8-GPU server with a 14 core CPU and 128GB memory. We exploit the stochastic gradient-based online learning, with a batch size of 64, to optimize model parameters. We apply the time-step dropout, which randomly sets several representations in the sequence to zeros with a probability of 0.2, on the word representations to avoid overfitting. We use the Adam algorithm to update the parameters with a constant learning rate $1 \times 10^{-3}$ , and apply the gradient clipping by a maximum value of 5.0 to avoid gradient explosion.
